gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau has curves that stay open-ended and a lowercase that sits just under its capitals, like a plain sans should. And over a full page of text, Woodgod's vintage, commanding heading gives way to a body that goes down easily.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Woodgod comes in loud, vintage and commanding, with tall lowercase. Noto Sans PhagsPa then takes over with see-through c shapes and a gentle step up to capitals, so the headline gets the swagger and the text gets the calm.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-phoenici: Loud, vintage and a bit swaggering. Woodgod carries the heading with wide channels into its bowls, while Noto Sans Phoenician follows with s curves opening wide at both ends and a generous lowercase height.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-psalter-: Woodgod's wide channels cut into every bowl, giving the heading a commanding, vintage voice. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi follows with gaping e shapes and barely rising capitals, a plain sans that keeps a long passage moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Wide, glass-porthole counters make Noto Sans Rejang look open at a glance, with clear gaps in c, e, s and a. Noto Sans Rejang is a sans-serif that would carry a long passage with little effort, under Woodgod's vintage heading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-runic: Woodgod's lowercase rises nearly to the capitals, and a wide channel leads into every bowl, so the heading looks commanding and old-school. Noto Sans Runic has a big x-height and curves that never close up, so a size slightly under the heading's looks right.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-samarita: Noto Sans Samaritan is a hefty, approachable plain sans, its curves holding plenty of daylight inside. Woodgod does the loud, vintage heading work; the body font simply does the reading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-saurasht: Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps its capitals barely taller than the lowercase around them, with counters that stay connected to the outside. And over a longer passage that gives the text a smooth, unfussy run beneath Woodgod's vintage, commanding heading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sc: Woodgod brings a commanding, vintage heading with tall lowercase and wide channels into its bowls. But Noto Sans SC stays quiet, with chalk-like curves and low ascenders, so a long stretch of body text reads smoothly.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Those wide channels into every bowl are what make Woodgod look so vintage and commanding. Noto Sans Sharada is the quieter one, a sans-serif with bulky lowercase and open c forms that never close into rings.
